data.title: Network Topology Inferable From Public Sources
data.summary:
Routing data, address allocations, reverse DNS naming and public peering records permit
the organisation's network structure, supplier dependencies and site locations to be
reconstructed without any active scanning.
data.description:
Routing and allocation data is public by design and cannot be withdrawn. What it reveals
is the shape of the estate: which ranges belong to the organisation, which transit and
cloud providers it depends on, and — through reverse DNS naming conventions — frequently
the function and location of individual hosts.

Naming is the controllable part. Reverse records that encode site, role and environment
convert an address range into an annotated map, and they are usually set that way for
operational convenience without the external consequence being considered.

Supplier dependencies derived from routing also inform supply chain targeting, which is
why this exposure matters beyond reconnaissance of the organisation itself.
data.recommendation:
* Review reverse DNS naming so records do not encode site, role or environment.
* Accept that allocation and routing data is public, and ensure the hosts it points at are
  hardened on that assumption.
* Include the supplier dependencies visible in routing data in supply chain risk
  assessment.
data.short_recommendation: Stop encoding site and role in reverse DNS; assume routing data is public.
